mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 2.0% signals an easing monetary cycle, compressing discount rates applied to equity cash flows and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained drop in the unemployment rate below 3.5% triggers positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as lower unemployment signals stronger labor market conditions and improved corporate earnings prospects.
failure_condition: If UNRATE does not fall below 3.5, or if 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rise in demand (GDPC1) coupled with a decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals contractionary monetary policy, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS rises while GDPC1 also rises, or if 20-day returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a strong labor market regime, sustained increases in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) above 150,000 and falling unemployment rates (UNRATE) below 3.5% signal robust employment and low inflation, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the regime conditions (PAYEMS ≤150000 or UNRATE ≥3.5) are not met, or if 60-day returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the supply index (INDPRO) above 110 signals stronger production capacity and balanced supply-demand dynamics, leading to positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate sustained growth.
failure_condition: If INDPRO does not exceed 110, or if 20-day returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 3.5% signals weakening labor market conditions, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate economic slowdown and reduced corporate profits.
failure_condition: If UNRATE does not rise above 3.5, or if 20-day returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous rises in both demand (GDPC1) and demand-related economic activity (RSAFS) above their 4-month moving averages signal robust economic growth, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 returns as market expectations for earnings expansion rise.
failure_condition: If either GDPC1 or RSAFS does not rise above their 4-month averages, or if 60-day returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During an easing monetary cycle regime, a sustained decline in the federal funds rate below 2.0% for 10 days triggers positive 5-day S&P 500 returns as investors anticipate future rate cuts and improved economic conditions.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS does not remain below 2.0 for 10 days, or if 5-day returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
